analysis:
Examined scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (base text, lines 1-869) and the patch excerpt. Changes are limited to a test assertion at ~line 730, where the route-lane regex for cluster-release-checks no longer requires a trailing ' required' token, and to a few comments (lines 720-721, 811-814) and an assertion at ~line 828 whose patch excerpt is truncated. The file is an offline CI workflow structure test and does not touch provider runtime code, the WebSocket contract, attestation, key custody, the cache (T-041), or any consumed authorization. Production security properties (TB-002/003/007/009/011, T-053/T-054) are not affected by this diff.

The only security-relevant consideration is CI-integrity posture: relaxing the regex means the test no longer pins that the macOS release-build-check lane is 'required' in the route. Per the comments, this reflects a new scheduling mode where the lane may be requested without a size or may fall back when job sizes are off. Whether that weakens a required gate, or whether the provider-plan.yml and route-script change that goes with it keeps cluster-release-checks mandatory through provider-test-gate (needs list asserted at line 269), is outside the supplied evidence. provider-test-gate still lists cluster-release-checks in needs and the UNIT/CLUSTER result checks remain, so the gate itself is unchanged in these units. I raise no finding. The remaining question is whether the companion workflow and route-script changes (provider-plan.yml, scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py), not supplied here, preserve the 'required' semantics for runner routing. Line 828's patch is truncated, so that change was not fully visible.
